# Step 87: 原研究交接

状态：Reflect（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

Step 87 began by accepting the Step 86 handoff but immediately incorporating the Strategist's correction. I sent session-group message #606 to alert A03 and A01 that the Sambusetti--BCG route may change the negative branch: for M=N#N with N closed real-hyperbolic, all-sign Einstein nonexistence is entropy-certified, and the quantitative question is whether Ricci defects can be driven down at the O(1/chi(N)) rate. I then searched Knowledge for Sambusetti, Besson--Courtois--Gallot, minimal entropy, connected sums, and LeBrun's footnote. I read LeBrun `Four-Manifolds without Einstein Metrics` lines 220--311, especially the footnote at lines 269--270, which states that Sambusetti used BCG entropy inequalities to show that the connected sum of two copies of any real-hyperbolic 4-manifold admits no Einstein metric while satisfying strict Hitchin--Thorpe. I read the Simplicial Volume Manifold Atlas lines 190--309 for the Ricci/simplicial-volume context, hyperbolic proportionality, and connected-sum additivity. Focused knowledge requests for Sambusetti 1996/1998 and BCG were only partially successful: the primary Sambusetti article was not acquired in full, but the search recovered exact bibliographic identities, including C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 322 (1996), 1213--1218 and Math. Ann. 311 (1998), 533--547, DOI 10.1007/s002080050199, and returned several usable full-text secondary or later theorem sources.

The key full-text source read was Kotschick `Entropies, Volumes, and Einstein Metrics` lines 1--260. It gives Theorem 1: for a closed oriented Einstein 4-manifold X, \(\chi(X)\ge\frac32|\sigma(X)|+\lambda(X)^4/(108\pi^2)\), with equality cases restricted to flat, non-flat locally Calabi--Yau, or constant negative curvature metrics. Lines 213--226 give Corollary 3 attributed to Sambusetti: if X admits a nonzero-degree map of degree d to a closed real-hyperbolic 4-manifold Y, then \(\chi(X)\ge\frac32|\sigma(X)|+|d|\chi(Y)\), equality only if X is real hyperbolic; the proof uses BCG's entropy-degree inequality \(\lambda(X)^4\ge d\,3^4\operatorname{Vol}(Y)\) and the hyperbolic Gauss--Bonnet identity \(\operatorname{Vol}(Y)=4\pi^2\chi(Y)/3\). I also read Bessières--Besson--Courtois--Gallot `Differentiable rigidity under Ricci curvature lower bound` lines 1--220, especially Theorems 1.1 and 1.5: for a nonzero-degree map to a closed hyperbolic n-manifold, any metric satisfying \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(n-1)g\) has volume at least degree times the hyperbolic volume, with equality only for a Riemannian covering; Corollary 1.7 states that for fixed hyperbolic X, any \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(n-1)g\) metric on X#X satisfies \(\operatorname{vol}\ge2(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{vol}(X)\). I read Connell--Dai--Nunez-Zimbron--Perales--Suarez-Serrato--Wei RCD entropy lines 57--130 as further confirmation of the entropy-degree framework and intermediate-cover/Sambusetti machinery, and Brunnbauer--Ishida--Suarez-Serrato lines 1--220 for the minimal-volume-entropy Einstein inequality and its relation to Sambusetti. Pieroni's thesis lines 780--1009 and grep results around 1229 showed connected-sum entropy upper-bound technology in dimension 3; it is useful analogy but not the 4D Sambusetti obstruction.

I audited the BF closed-to-relative interface from Step 86 in parallel. I reread Iida--Mukherjee--Taniguchi lines 1--130, 200--269, and 500--544. The source explicitly states Theorem 1.1: nonzero \(\Psi(W,\xi,\mathfrak{s})\) forbids non-torsion classes in \(H_2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)\) represented by embedded 2-spheres with nonnegative square; Theorem 3.1(ii) gives the same genus-zero assertion; Theorem 4.6 gives the relative BF version for rational-homology-sphere homotopy-L-space boundary and b1(W)=0; and lines 512--520 list the gluing computations BF(D4)=Id, BF(X^o)=BF(X), and connected-sum composition. This supports the conclusion that the standard closed BF invariants used by Ishida--LeBrun, once viewed through the punctured relative interface with boundary S3, cannot coexist with the non-torsion +2 spheres inserted by reversed A1 nodes. I did not write the promised durable BF note or patch Step 85 because the finalization signal arrived, but the corrected scope is now clear.

I read the relevant parts of Step 85's reduction note and identified exact patches needed. Section 1's Corollary 1.1 overstates the high-dimensional conclusion: the Lohkamp argument gives a necessary prerequisite for refutation, while 'no no-Einstein manifold known for n>=5' is only current source status, not a theorem forbidding n>=5 inquiry. Section 8 overstates negative-side disjointness by implying a class-level monopole/BF incompatibility; it must instead say positive pinching is class-level SW/BF-disjoint by PSC, whereas on the negative side the disjointness only concerns our A1 construction machine and known BF/monopole certificates. Section 13's item about no negative-Einstein obstruction compatible with PSC/SW-void mixed rows remains true for the simply connected mixed rows but is no longer a global statement about negative reservoirs, because Sambusetti/BCG gives a homotopy/entropy reservoir with infinite fundamental group. I also received A03 #607 requesting the exact Sambusetti theorem and A01 #609 clarifying the K-symmetry/local Green coefficient scope. I did not yet reply to #607 with source paths; that should be done next after the theorem note is written. No branch of Yau--26 was solved, refuted, or Lean-formalized in this step.

## 当时的后续问题

Turn the Step 87 audit into a precise mathematical object and repair the shared reduction record. First write a durable note, e.g. `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/notes/step88_sambusetti_bcg_negative_branch_audit.md`, with theorem-level statements and exact source paths: LeBrun footnote in `Knowledge/objects/papers/Four-Manifolds-without-Einstein-Metrics--5b090e14de27--d63c56d541e8/object.md` lines 269--270; Kotschick `Entropies, Volumes, and Einstein Metrics` lines 156--226 for the Einstein entropy inequality and Sambusetti corollary; Bessières--Besson--Courtois--Gallot lines 31--34, 67--81, and 91--99 for the Ricci-lower-bound volume theorem and X#X gap; Simplicial Volume Atlas lines 286--292 for connected-sum additivity; and Iida--Mukherjee--Taniguchi lines 35--40, 246--260, 512--520, and 523--535 for the BF relative adjunction/closed-to-punctured audit. Be explicit that the primary Sambusetti paper itself was not acquired in full during Step 87; either retrieve it in a fresh focused request or mark the source state honestly while using Kotschick/BBCG as the exact theorem source.

Second, patch `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/notes/step85_yau26_established_reduction.md` without weakening the target. Section 1 should say the Lohkamp theorem gives a necessary prerequisite for any refutation in dimension n>=3: if every closed n-manifold had some Einstein metric, the interval [c,0] would prove Yau--26 in that dimension. The n>=5 statement must be current search/literature status only, not a theorem. Add a new section for the hyperbolic connected-sum family \(M_N=N\#N\): \(\chi(M_N)=2\chi(N)-2\), \(\tau=0\), degree-2 map to N, positive simplicial volume, strict Hitchin--Thorpe, and no Einstein metric of any sign by Sambusetti/Kotschick.

For a metric on \(M_N\) with \(\|\operatorname{Ric}+3g\|_{op}\le\delta\), record exactly how scaling gives a Ricci-lower-bound metric to which BBCG applies: from \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(3+\delta)g\), scale by \(1+\delta/3\) to get \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-3\hat g\), hence \(\operatorname{Vol}_g(M_N)\ge 2\operatorname{Vol}(N)/(1+\delta/3)^2\), with a possible fixed-N strengthening by the BBCG X#X gap. Combine this with a sharp Chern--Gauss--Bonnet upper bound using eigenvalues \(-3+\eta_i\), \(|\eta_i|\le\delta\): compute lower bounds for \(s^2/24-|E|^2/2\), obtain an explicit \(\operatorname{Vol}_g\le 8\pi^2\chi(M_N)/D(\delta)\), and solve for a rigorous lower bound \(\delta\ge c/\chi(N)+O(\chi(N)^{-2})\) for near-negative pinching on \(N\#N\). ## 已开展的研究

Step 88 built the three structural results that Step 87 identified but did not write. (1) WARPED-PRODUCT WAIST BARRIER: proved that for warped product g=dr²+f(r)²g_F with Einstein 3-fiber Ric_F=2kg_F, at any waist (f'=0, f''≥0), the Ricci defect from -3 satisfies δ≥3/2 when k≥0, equality only at k=0, α=f''/f=3/2. For round S³: δ=3/2+3/(2f₀²)>3/2 at every fiber scale. Verified computationally (`workspace/data/step88_warped_waist_and_bcg_threshold.json`). # Step 88: Sambusetti–BCG entropy obstruction, warped-product waist barrier, and resolution/simplicial-volume disjointness

Session `S0910A02`, Agent2/Constructor, Step 88.

This note records three structural results that reshape the negative-branch landscape of Yau–26 in dimension four: (1) the Sambusetti–BCG all-sign no-Einstein family and its quantitative pinching threshold, (2) a pointwise waist obstruction preventing warped-product near-pinching on connected sums, and (3) the decisive topological question about whether any A₁-resolution can access the entropy-obstructed reservoir.

---

## 1. Sambusetti–BCG all-sign no-Einstein family

**Sources.** LeBrun's footnote in `Knowledge/objects/papers/Four-Manifolds-without-Einstein-Metrics--5b090e14de27--d63c56d541e8/object.md`, lines 269–270; Kotschick `Knowledge/objects/papers/Entropies-Volumes-and-Einstein-Metrics--a5cc2bf9d68e--94203f883336/object.md`, Theorem 1 and Corollary 3 (lines 156–226); Bessières–Besson–Courtois–Gallot `Knowledge/objects/papers/Differentiable-rigidity-under-Ricci-curvature-lower-bound--cfb4c9cdd3c7--65a5a48bd00c/object.md`, Theorems 1.1, 1.5, Corollary 1.7. The primary Sambusetti source (Math. Ann. 311, 1998, 533–547, DOI 10.1007/s002080050199) was not fully retrieved.

**Setup.** Let $N^4$ be a closed oriented real-hyperbolic 4-manifold with sectional curvature $-1$:
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_0} = -3g_0, \qquad
\operatorname{Vol}(N,g_0) = \frac{4\pi^2}{3}\chi(N), \qquad
\tau(N) = 0.
$$
The connected sum $M_N = N \# N$ has:
$$
\chi(M_N) = 2\chi(N) - 2, \qquad
\tau(M_N) = 0, \qquad
\|M_N\| = 2\|N\| > 0.
$$
There is a degree-two continuous map $f: M_N \to N$ obtained by collapsing one punctured summand to a point and mapping the other by the identity.

**Theorem (Sambusetti, via Kotschick/BCG).** *$M_N$ admits no Einstein metric of any sign.*

*Proof.* By Kotschick Corollary 3, any closed oriented Einstein 4-manifold $X$ admitting a nonzero-degree map $f: X \to Y$ to a closed real-hyperbolic manifold $Y$ satisfies:
$$
\chi(X) \ge \frac{3}{2}|\sigma(X)| + |\deg f| \, \chi(Y),
$$
with equality only if $X$ is real-hyperbolic. For $M_N$ with $\deg f = 2$:
$$
2\chi(N) - 2 \ge 0 + 2\chi(N)
$$
is impossible. $\square$

**Observations.** (a) This is NOT a gauge-theoretic obstruction: it uses the Besson–Courtois–Gallot entropy inequality and homotopy degree, not monopole classes, SW invariants, or BF invariants. (b) The family has $\chi > 0$, $\tau = 0$, and strict Hitchin–Thorpe $(2\chi - 2 > 3|\tau| = 0)$ for $\chi(N) \ge 2$. (c) The manifolds are not simply connected: $\pi_1(M_N)$ is a free product with one relation from the hyperbolic lattice. (d) The positive simplicial volume $\|M_N\| > 0$ obstructs $\lambda \ge 0$ independently: any metric with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge 0$ forces simplicial volume zero by the Cheeger–Gromoll/Bishop–Gromov mechanism, contradicting $\|M_N\| > 0$.

---

## 2. BCG extension to Ricci-lower-bound metrics and quantitative pinching threshold

**Theorem (BCG lower bound, metric-level).** For any metric $g$ on $M_N$ with $\operatorname{Ric}_g \ge -(n-1)g$ (with $n = 4$: $\operatorname{Ric}_g \ge -3g$):
$$
\operatorname{Vol}(M_N, g) \ge 2 \, \operatorname{Vol}(N, g_0).
$$
Equality implies $g$ is isometric to $g_0$ on each summand. Corollary 1.7 of BBCG: for fixed $N$, there exists $\varepsilon_N > 0$ such that
$$
\operatorname{Vol}_g(M_N) \ge 2(1 + \varepsilon_N) \operatorname{Vol}(N)
$$
for all metrics with $\operatorname{Ric}_g \ge -3g$.

**Source:** BBCG Theorem 1.5 (lines 67–81) and Corollary 1.7 (lines 91–99). This uses only $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -3g$, not the Einstein equation.

**CGB upper bound under two-sided negative Ricci pinching.** Suppose
$$
-3(1+\varepsilon)g \le \operatorname{Ric}_g \le -3(1-\varepsilon)g, \qquad 0 < \varepsilon < 1.
$$
Let $r_i = -3x_i$ be the Ricci eigenvalues with $x_i \in [1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]$. The CGB integrand satisfies:
$$
\frac{s^2}{6} - \frac{|\operatorname{Ric}|^2}{2}
= \frac{3}{2}\bigl[(\textstyle\sum x_i)^2 - 3\sum x_i^2\bigr].
$$
This quadratic is concave in each variable; its minimum on the box $[1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]^4$ occurs at the vertex $x_1 = \cdots = x_4 = 1-\varepsilon$ for $\varepsilon \le 1/2$, giving:
$$
\frac{s^2}{6} - \frac{|\operatorname{Ric}|^2}{2} \ge 6(1-\varepsilon)^2.
$$
(Note: A01's message #610–611 uses an intermediate formula $(3/2)[(\sum x)^2/3 - \sum x^2]$, which has a factor-of-3 error in the first term. The final bound $6(1-\varepsilon)^2$ is nevertheless correct. See `workspace/data/step88_warped_waist_and_bcg_threshold.json`.)

**CGB gives:**
$$
8\pi^2(2\chi(N)-2) \ge 6(1-\varepsilon)^2 \operatorname{Vol}(M_N, g),
$$
hence
$$
\operatorname{Vol}(M_N, g) \le \frac{2\operatorname{Vol}(N)(1 - 1/\chi(N))}{(1-\varepsilon)^2}.
$$

**Rescaling for BCG.** If $\|\operatorname{Ric}_g + 3g\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \delta$, set $\varepsilon = \delta/3$. Then $\operatorname{Ric}_g \ge -(3+\delta)g$. Scale $\hat g = (1 + \delta/3)g$: then $\operatorname{Ric}_{\hat g} = \operatorname{Ric}_g \ge -3\hat g$ and $\operatorname{Vol}_{\hat g} = (1+\delta/3)^2 \operatorname{Vol}_g$.

BCG lower bound applied to $\hat g$:
$$
\operatorname{Vol}_g \ge \frac{2\operatorname{Vol}(N)}{(1+\varepsilon)^2}.
$$

**Volume incompatibility.** The lower and upper bounds are incompatible when:
$$
\left(\frac{1-\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}\right)^2 > 1 - \frac{1}{\chi(N)}.
$$

**Threshold:**
$$
\varepsilon < \varepsilon_\chi := \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - 1/\chi(N)}}{1 + \sqrt{1 - 1/\chi(N)}} = \frac{1}{4\chi(N)} + O(\chi(N)^{-2}).
$$
In operator norm: $\delta < 3\varepsilon_\chi \approx \frac{3}{4\chi(N)}$.

**Meaning.** This is an additive certificate: the volume deficit arises from the constant $\chi(M_N) = 2\chi(N) - 2$ versus $2\chi(N)$, an additive gap of 2. No additive certificate can produce a uniform $\delta_0 > 0$ independent of $N$, because the critical rate goes to zero as $\chi(N) \to \infty$. This means the entropy obstruction *prices* a refutation of $P_4^-$ at rate $O(1/\chi)$ but cannot *close* the branch.

**Weyl budget at critical rate:** when $\delta \sim 1/\chi(N)$, the Weyl curvature integral satisfies $\int |W|^2 = O(1)$, an extremely tight scale-invariant budget.

---

## 3. Warped-product waist obstruction

**Theorem (waist barrier, $k \ge 0$).** *For a warped product $g = dr^2 + f(r)^2 g_F$ on $\mathbb{R} \times F^3$ with $\operatorname{Ric}_F = 2k\, g_F$ and $k \ge 0$ (flat or positively curved fiber): at any waist $r_0$ where $f'(r_0) = 0$, $f''(r_0) \ge 0$, the Ricci endomorphism defect from $-3$ satisfies*
$$
\delta := \max\bigl(|\lambda_r + 3|, |\lambda_F + 3|\bigr) \ge \frac{3}{2},
$$
*with equality if and only if $k = 0$ and $f''(r_0)/f(r_0) = 3/2$.*

*Proof.* At the waist, the Ricci endomorphism eigenvalues are:
$$
\lambda_r = -3\alpha, \qquad \lambda_F = \beta - \alpha,
$$
where $\alpha = f''/f \ge 0$ and $\beta = 2k/f^2 \ge 0$. The defects from $-3$ are:
$$
\delta_r = 3|1 - \alpha|, \qquad \delta_F = |3 - \alpha + \beta|.
$$
For $\alpha \le 1$: $\delta_F = 3 - \alpha + \beta \ge 2$ (since $\beta \ge 0$, $\alpha \le 1$).
For $1 \le \alpha \le 3$: equalize $3(\alpha - 1) = 3 - \alpha + \beta \Rightarrow \alpha = (6 + \beta)/4$, $\delta = 3(\beta + 2)/4$. For $\beta = 0$: $\alpha = 3/2$, $\delta = 3/2$. For $\beta > 0$: $\delta > 3/2$.
For $\alpha > 3$: $\delta_r > 6$ and $\delta_F = \alpha - 3 + \beta - \alpha = \beta - 3$ or $3 - \alpha + \beta < 0$... In fact, for $\alpha > 3$ and $\beta \ge 0$: $\delta_r = 3(\alpha - 1) > 6$, always worse.

Hence $\inf_{\alpha \ge 0, \beta \ge 0} \delta = 3/2$, achieved at $\alpha = 3/2$, $\beta = 0$.

For the round $S^3$ fiber ($k = 1$): $\beta = 2/f_0^2 > 0$, so $\delta = 3/2 + 3/(2f_0^2) > 3/2$, approaching $3/2$ only as $f_0 \to \infty$.

*Check.* Hyperbolic $\mathbb{H}^4$ in equidistant coordinates from $\mathbb{H}^3$: $f(r) = \cosh r$, $k = -1$, $\beta = -2$, $\alpha = 1$ at $r = 0$. Then $\lambda_r = -3$, $\lambda_F = -2 - 1 = -3$. Zero defect. $\checkmark$

*Check.* The cusp metric $f(r) = e^{-r}$, $k = 0$: $\alpha = 1$, $\beta = 0$, $(f'/f)^2 = 1$. $\lambda_r = -3$, $\lambda_F = 0 - 1 - 2 = -3$. Zero defect, but no waist (monotone $f$). $\checkmark$ $\square$

**Implication for connected-sum necks.** A connected sum $N \# N$ where $N$ is a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold has a separating $S^3$ waist (round fiber, $k = 1$). The waist barrier gives $\delta > 3/2$ at any warped-product turnaround, regardless of scale. This is a **pointwise** obstruction: it cannot be amortized over large volume, unlike the CGB energy accounting. It explains why A03's monotone-functional search found no construction: in the warped-product class, a cusp-to-cusp turnaround through $S^3$ or $T^3$ is locally forbidden below $\delta = 3/2$.

**General (non-warped) waists.** For a minimal separating hypersurface $\Sigma^3$ in $(M^4, g)$ with $\operatorname{Ric} \approx -3g$, the traced Gauss equation gives:
$$
\operatorname{Scal}_\Sigma = -6 - |A|^2 + O(\delta).
$$
This does not yield a contradiction since any closed 3-manifold admits metrics of arbitrarily negative scalar curvature. A general "no near-pinched $S^3$ or $T^3$ waist" theorem would be a stronger statement and would kill both known negative reservoirs (LeBrun blow-ups and Sambusetti sums are both connected sums).

---

## 4. Chern–Weil neutrality and entropy inaccessibility

*Corrected in Step 90. The original Step 88 §4.1 incorrectly claimed the negative mirror has infinite $\pi_1$ with abelianization $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^8$. Step 57 van Kampen proves all fillings are simply connected. The entropy-access criteria of §4.2–4.3 are superseded by the BCG inaccessibility theorem below.*

### 4.1 Correction: both mirrors are simply connected

Step 57 proved by van Kampen that every sign-pattern filling of both mirrors is simply connected. Each EH cap has $\pi_1(\mathrm{EH}) = 1$ and kills the $\mathbb{Z}/2$ peripheral group of the $\mathrm{RP}^3$ boundary. With many stabilizer normal closures, the filling relations annihilate all remaining torsion — the same mechanism that makes Kummer K3 simply connected from $T^4/\mathbb{Z}_2$ with 16 nodes.

The coinvariant-only shortcut omitted 35 (resp. 3) extra filling relations. The self-contradiction was visible: if $\iota_*$ inverts every element, then every element in the coinvariant quotient satisfies $\gamma = \gamma^{-1}$, making it abelian and finite — and the filling relations collapse it to the trivial group.

**Standing caution (seam compression).** $\mathrm{RP}^3$ boundaries are amenable seams. Filling them with simply-connected EH caps compresses the fundamental group. The relative simplicial volume $\|(X_0, \partial X_0)\|$ of the complement may be positive, but amenable-boundary additivity requires $\pi_1$-injective seams. EH caps violate this, so $\|M\| = 0$ despite $\|(X_0, \partial)\| > 0$. Sources: Bargagnati–Frigerio Proposition 2.3; Bucher–Burger–Frigerio–Iozzi–Pagliantini–Pozzetti Theorem 2.1.

### 4.2 Chern–Weil neutrality of Ricci-flat ALE bubbles

**Theorem (ALE non-decrease).** *For any Ricci-flat ALE 4-space, $|\Delta\tau| \le \frac{2}{3}\,\Delta\chi$ with equality iff half-flat. Hence for any orbifold+Ricci-flat-ALE resolution:*
$$
\chi(M) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O})|.
$$

*Proof.* Since $\operatorname{Ric} = 0$: $|12\pi^2\,\Delta\tau| = |\int(|W^+|^2 - |W^-|^2)| \le \int |W|^2 = 8\pi^2\,\Delta\chi$, giving $|\Delta\tau| \le \frac{2}{3}\,\Delta\chi$. Triangle inequality on $\tau(M) = \tau_{\mathrm{orb}} + \sum \Delta\tau_i$ gives $|\tau(M)| \le |\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}| + \frac{2}{3}\sum \Delta\chi_i$. Subtracting: $\chi(M) - \frac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge \chi_{\mathrm{orb}} - \frac{3}{2}|\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}|$. $\square$

For the Eguchi–Hanson: $\Delta\chi = 3/2$, $|\Delta\tau| = 1$, ratio $= 2/3$ exactly. Verified on 15 examples including K3 (equality at surplus 0), positive mirror (equality at aligned $r=0,4$; strict at mixed $r=1,2,3$), negative mirror (equality at aligned; strict at balanced), and both Davis involutions. Data: `workspace/data/step90_chernweil_neutrality_verification.json`.

### 4.3 Entropy inaccessibility (answers §4.3 of original Step 88 decisively)

**Theorem (Entropy inaccessibility).** *For any smooth $A_1$ resolution $M$ of any closed real-hyperbolic 4-orbifold $\mathcal{O}$ with isolated $A_1$ points, and any degree-$d \ne 0$ map $f: M \to Y$ ($Y$ closed hyperbolic):*
$$
d \cdot \chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}).
$$
*Hence the Sambusetti inequality is automatically satisfied and no entropy certificate can obstruct Einstein metrics on $M$.*

*Proof.* The near-pinched construction (Theorem 5) gives metrics $g_a$ on $M$ with $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_a} \ge -(3+\varepsilon_a)g_a$, $\varepsilon_a \to 0$, and $\operatorname{Vol}(g_a) \to \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O})$. Rescaling: $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -3\hat g$ with $\operatorname{Vol}(\hat g) \to \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O})$. BCG (BBCG Thm 1.1): $d \cdot \operatorname{Vol}(Y) \le \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O})$. Converting via $\chi = \frac{3}{4\pi^2}\operatorname{Vol}$: $d\cdot\chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}$. By non-decrease: $\chi(M) - \frac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge \chi_{\mathrm{orb}} \ge d\cdot\chi(Y)$. $\square$

This answers the original decisive question **NEGATIVELY for ALL orbifold+ALE resolutions.** No $\pi_1$ computation, simplicial-volume estimate, or degree-map topology is needed. The BCG volume bound from the near-pinched metrics closes the entire entropy route at once.

### 4.4 Triple disjointness

All three known families of no-Einstein certificates are independently blind to the audited near-pinched orbifold+ALE construction:

1. **PSC/Weitzenböck $\perp$ monopole/BF** (positive, class-level): positive Ric pinching $\Rightarrow$ PSC $\Rightarrow$ Weitzenböck kills SW/BF.
2. **IMT adjunction $\perp$ reversed $A_1$ nodes** (negative, construction-class): reversed nodes insert $+2$-spheres $\Rightarrow$ IMT kills BF.
3. **Chern–Weil neutrality $\perp$ entropy** (all signs, all orbifold+ALE): half-flat ALE: $\Delta(\chi - \frac{3}{2}|\tau|) = 0$; BCG: $d\cdot\chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}$. Sambusetti always satisfied.

A refutation must either construct near-pinched metrics outside orbifold+ALE (non-warped connector), or discover a no-Einstein mechanism outside all three shields. Full analysis: `workspace/notes/step90_chernweil_neutrality_and_triple_disjointness.md`.

---

## 5. Implications for the negative branch $P_4^-$

The negative-branch landscape is now:

| Family | No-Einstein mechanism | Near-pinching status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| $N \# N$, $N$ hyperbolic | Sambusetti/BCG entropy | $\delta \ge 3/(4\chi(N))$; warped $S^3$ waist: $\delta \ge 3/2$ | Non-warped waists remain open |
| $X \# k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2$, LeBrun | BF/monopole | Burns core $O(1)$ defect | A₁ machine disjoint from this reservoir |
| Negative mirror mixed rows | Unknown | $\delta \le C/|\log a|$ by A₁ construction | Entropy invisible ($\|M\| = 0$) |
| Hyp. orbifold $A_1$ resolution | Sambusetti (inaccessible) | $\delta \le C/|\log a|$ (exists, e.g. Davis) | §4.3 answered NO: Chern–Weil neutrality + BCG |

**Current state of $P_4^-$:**
- Warped-product methods cannot produce near-negative-pinched connected sums ($\delta \ge 3/2$ at waists).
- The CGB/BCG threshold $\delta \sim 1/\chi(N)$ is additive and cannot produce a uniform $\delta_0$.
- The A₁ construction machine produces $\delta \to 0$ metrics, but on manifolds that are currently entropy-invisible.
- Question 4.3 is answered negatively (§4.3): Chern–Weil neutrality + BCG volume comparison prove entropy inaccessibility for ALL orbifold+ALE resolutions. Refuting $P_4^-$ requires a non-warped connector at rate $O(1/\chi)$ or a new no-Einstein mechanism outside all three disjointness shields.

---

~~~~python
"""
Step 88: Warped-product waist obstruction and BCG pinching threshold.

Part 1: For g = dr^2 + f(r)^2 g_F on I x F^3, with Ric_F = 2k g_F,
Ricci endomorphism eigenvalues at a waist (f'=0, f''>=0):
  lambda_r = -3 f''/f = -3 alpha
  lambda_F = 2k/f^2 - f''/f = beta - alpha

For Ric approx -3g, defects:
  delta_r = |lambda_r + 3| = 3|1 - alpha|
  delta_F = |lambda_F + 3| = |beta - alpha + 3|

Minimize max(delta_r, delta_F) over alpha >= 0, beta >= 0 (k >= 0).

Part 2: BCG/CGB pinching threshold for N#N.
"""

import json
import numpy as np

results = {}

# ============================================================
# Part 1: Warped-product waist obstruction
# ============================================================

def waist_defect(alpha, beta):
    """Max Ricci defect from -3 at a waist with alpha=f''/f, beta=2k/f^2."""
    dr = 3 * abs(1 - alpha)
    dF = abs(beta - alpha + 3)
    return max(dr, dF)

# For k=0 (flat T^3 fiber): beta = 0
# Optimal: equalize 3|1-alpha| = |3-alpha| for alpha in [0, inf)
# Case alpha <= 1: 3(1-alpha) = 3-alpha -> alpha=0, delta=3
# Case 1 <= alpha <= 3: 3(alpha-1) = 3-alpha -> 4alpha=6 -> alpha=3/2, delta=3/2
# Case alpha >= 3: 3(alpha-1) = alpha-3 -> 2alpha=0, impossible
alpha_opt_k0 = 1.5
beta_opt_k0 = 0.0
delta_k0 = waist_defect(alpha_opt_k0, beta_opt_k0)

# Numerical verification: scan alpha in [0, 5] with beta=0
alpha_grid = np.linspace(0, 5, 10001)
defects_k0 = [waist_defect(a, 0) for a in alpha_grid]
delta_k0_num = min(defects_k0)
alpha_k0_num = alpha_grid[np.argmin(defects_k0)]

results["k0_flat_fiber"] = {
    "alpha_optimal": alpha_opt_k0,
    "beta_optimal": beta_opt_k0,
    "delta_exact": 1.5,
    "delta_numeric": round(delta_k0_num, 10),
    "alpha_numeric": round(alpha_k0_num, 6),
    "match": abs(delta_k0 - 1.5) < 1e-12 and abs(delta_k0_num - 1.5) < 1e-4,
}

# For k=1 (round S^3 fiber): beta = 2/f_0^2 > 0
# Equalize 3(alpha-1) = beta - alpha + 3 -> alpha = (beta+6)/4
# delta = 3((beta+6)/4 - 1) = 3(beta+2)/4
# As f_0 -> inf: beta -> 0, delta -> 3/2 from above
f0_values = [1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100, 1e6]
k1_data = []
for f0 in f0_values:
    beta = 2.0 / f0**2
    alpha = (beta + 6) / 4
    delta = 3 * (beta + 2) / 4
    # Numeric check
    defects_k1 = [waist_defect(a, beta) for a in alpha_grid]
    delta_num = min(defects_k1)
    k1_data.append({
        "f0": f0, "beta": round(beta, 12),
        "alpha_opt": round(alpha, 10), "delta_exact": round(delta, 10),
        "delta_numeric": round(delta_num, 10),
        "delta_exceeds_1.5": delta > 1.5,
    })
results["k1_round_fiber"] = {
    "formula": "delta = 3(2/f0^2 + 2)/4 = 3/2 + 3/(2 f0^2)",
    "limit_f0_to_inf": 1.5,
    "samples": k1_data,
}

# For k=-1 (hyperbolic H^3 fiber): beta = -2/f_0^2 < 0
# Check H^4 equidistant from H^3: f(r) = cosh(r), at r=0: alpha=1, beta=-2
# lambda_r = -3, lambda_F = -2-1 = -3. Defect = 0.
alpha_H4 = 1.0
beta_H4 = -2.0
delta_H4 = waist_defect(alpha_H4, beta_H4)
results["km1_hyperbolic_fiber"] = {
    "H4_equidistant": {
        "f_0": 1, "alpha": alpha_H4, "beta": beta_H4,
        "delta": delta_H4,
        "note": "H4 equidistant from H3, zero defect",
    },
    "conclusion": "Negatively curved fiber permits defect-free waist; "
                   "this is the H4 metric itself, hence Einstein.",
}

# Summary
results["waist_summary"] = {
    "theorem": (
        "For a warped product g = dr^2 + f(r)^2 g_F on R x F^3 with "
        "Ric_F = 2k g_F: at any waist (f'=0, f''>=0), the Ricci "
        "endomorphism defect from -3 satisfies delta >= 3/2 when k >= 0 "
        "(flat or positively curved fiber). Equality holds when k=0 and "
        "f''/f = 3/2. For k < 0, zero defect is achieved by the "
        "hyperbolic metric. Connected sums N#N have S^3 waists (k=1), "
        "giving delta > 3/2 at every warped-product turnaround."
    ),
    "delta_flat_T3": 1.5,
    "delta_round_S3_any_radius": "> 1.5",
    "delta_hyperbolic_H3_optimal": 0.0,
    "implication": (
        "The warped-product class cannot produce near-negative-pinched "
        "metrics on connected sums or graph manifolds with positively "
        "curved or flat cross-sections. This is a pointwise obstruction, "
        "not an energy obstruction, and cannot be amortized over volume."
    ),
}

# ============================================================
# Part 2: BCG/CGB pinching threshold for N#N
# ============================================================

# CGB integrand lower bound under two-sided negative Ricci pinching
# Ric eigenvalues r_i = -3 x_i, x_i in [1-eps, 1+eps]
# s^2/6 - |Ric|^2/2 = (3/2)[(sum x_i)^2 - 3 sum x_i^2]
# NOTE: A01's intermediate formula (3/2)[(sum x)^2/3 - sum x^2] is WRONG
# by a factor of 3 in the first term. Correct is (3/2)[(sum x)^2 - 3 sum x^2].
# However, the final answer 6(1-eps)^2 is correct because all same-sign
# vertex gives sum x = 4(1-eps), sum x^2 = 4(1-eps)^2,
# so (3/2)[16(1-eps)^2 - 12(1-eps)^2] = (3/2)*4*(1-eps)^2 = 6(1-eps)^2.

def cgb_integrand_lower(eps):
    """CGB integrand s^2/6 - |Ric|^2/2 minimum for Ric eigs in [-3(1+eps), -3(1-eps)]."""
    # Minimum at all x_i = 1-eps (for eps < 1/2)
    S = 4 * (1 - eps)
    Q = 4 * (1 - eps)**2
    return 1.5 * (S**2 - 3 * Q)

# Verify at eps=0: should give 6
assert abs(cgb_integrand_lower(0) - 6.0) < 1e-12

# Cross-check the intermediate formula error
def a01_intermediate(eps):
    """A01's intermediate: (3/2)[(sum x)^2/3 - sum x^2] at all x=1-eps."""
    S = 4 * (1 - eps)
    Q = 4 * (1 - eps)**2
    return 1.5 * (S**2 / 3 - Q)

# At eps=0: A01 gives (3/2)[16/3 - 4] = (3/2)(4/3) = 2, not 6
a01_check = a01_intermediate(0)
correct_check = cgb_integrand_lower(0)

results["cgb_formula_check"] = {
    "correct_formula": "(3/2)[(sum x_i)^2 - 3 sum x_i^2]",
    "a01_intermediate": "(3/2)[(sum x_i)^2/3 - sum x_i^2]",
    "at_eps_0_correct": correct_check,
    "at_eps_0_a01": a01_check,
    "a01_intermediate_has_factor_3_error": True,
    "a01_final_answer_6_1_minus_eps_sq_is_correct": True,
    "note": "A01 got the right final answer despite wrong intermediate."
}

# Pinching threshold: incompatibility when
# (1-eps)^2/(1+eps)^2 > 1 - 1/chi(N)
# eps < eps_chi = (1 - sqrt(1-1/chi))/(1 + sqrt(1-1/chi))
chi_values = [2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000]
threshold_data = []
for chi in chi_values:
    sq = np.sqrt(1 - 1.0/chi)
    eps_chi = (1 - sq) / (1 + sq)
    delta_chi = 3 * eps_chi  # operator norm threshold
    # Leading order: eps ~ 1/(4*chi), delta ~ 3/(4*chi)
    eps_leading = 1.0 / (4 * chi)
    delta_leading = 3.0 / (4 * chi)
    threshold_data.append({
        "chi_N": chi, "eps_chi": round(eps_chi, 10),
        "delta_chi": round(delta_chi, 10),
        "eps_leading": round(eps_leading, 10),
        "delta_leading": round(delta_leading, 10),
        "ratio_to_leading": round(eps_chi / eps_leading, 6) if eps_leading > 0 else None,
    })

results["bcg_cgb_threshold"] = {
    "formula": "eps_chi = (1 - sqrt(1-1/chi))/(1 + sqrt(1-1/chi))",
    "operator_norm": "delta = 3*eps, threshold delta < 3/(4*chi) + O(chi^{-2})",
    "additive_certificate": True,
    "note": (
        "The volume deficit arises from chi(N#N) = 2*chi(N)-2, "
        "a fixed additive constant 8*pi^2/3. No additive certificate "
        "can produce a uniform delta_0 independent of N. Hence this "
        "obstruction prices the refutation at O(1/chi) but cannot "
        "close the negative branch."
    ),
    "data": threshold_data,
}

# At critical rate, Weyl energy constraint
# Vol ~ 2*Vol(N), CGB: 8*pi^2*(2*chi-2) = int(|W|^2 + 6)*Vol + O(delta)
# So int |W|^2 = 8*pi^2*(2*chi-2) - 6*Vol + O(delta*Vol)
# = 8*pi^2*(2*chi-2) - 6*2*(4*pi^2/3)*chi + O(delta*Vol)
# = 16*pi^2*chi - 16*pi^2 - 16*pi^2*chi + O(delta*Vol)
# = -16*pi^2 + O(delta*Vol) = O(1)
results["weyl_budget_at_critical_rate"] = {
    "note": (
        "At the critical pinching rate delta ~ 1/chi, with Vol ~ 2*Vol(N), "
        "the Weyl curvature integral is int|W|^2 = O(1), an extremely "
        "tight scale-invariant budget for any candidate metric."
    ),
}

# ============================================================
# Part 3: Gauss equation for minimal separating hypersurface
# ============================================================
# For minimal Sigma^3 in (M^4, g) with Ric ~ -3g:
# Scal_Sigma = Scal_M - 2*Ric(nu,nu) - |A|^2  (minimal: H=0)
# = (-12 + O(delta)) - 2*(-3 + O(delta)) - |A|^2
# = -6 - |A|^2 + O(delta)
# This is not a contradiction since any closed 3-manifold admits
# metrics with very negative scalar curvature.
results["gauss_equation_minimal"] = {
    "formula": "Scal_Sigma = -6 - |A|^2 + O(delta)",
    "note": "No contradiction from Gauss alone; non-warped waists remain open."
}

# Save
outpath = "Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step88_warped_waist_and_bcg_threshold.json"
with open(outpath, "w") as f:
    json.dump(results, f, indent=2, default=str)

print(f"Saved to {outpath}")
print(f"\nWarped waist k=0 delta = {delta_k0}")
print(f"CGB correct at eps=0: {correct_check}, A01 intermediate: {a01_check}")
print(f"Threshold at chi=100: eps={threshold_data[7]['eps_chi']}, delta={threshold_data[7]['delta_chi']}")
print(f"H4 equidistant defect: {delta_H4}")

# Step 89: 原研究交接

状态：Repair（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

Step 89 audited Step 88's requested structural claims rather than approving them. I read `workspace/notes/step88_sambusetti_bcg_waist_and_disjointness.md`, `workspace/data/step88_warped_waist_and_bcg_threshold.json`, the patched `workspace/notes/step85_yau26_established_reduction.md`, and the older `workspace/notes/step57_dichotomy_and_kahler_exclusion.md`. The waist barrier and BCG/CGB threshold remain sound: the data file records the k>=0 warped waist lower bound δ>=3/2, the round S3 sharpening, the H4 and cusp checks, and the corrected CGB formula. The serious defect is Step 88 §4.1: it claimed the negative mirror resolution has infinite π1 with abelianization (Z/2)^8. Step 57's van Kampen proof is stronger and correct: all 36-node sign-pattern fillings are simply connected because M0 is simply connected and both ±2 disk-bundle caps are simply connected while killing the RP3 boundary π1. The coinvariant-only shortcut omitted the extra relations from the 36 point stabilizers. This also invalidates Step 88 §4.2's suggested Betti-number criterion as a decisive entropy test.

I requested outside knowledge for the corrected Armstrong/simplicial-volume/hyperbolic-involution question. Retrieval was partial but useful. For Armstrong, I read Biswas--Hai--dos Santos lines 29--32, which quote Armstrong's theorem: for a simply connected locally compact metric space with discontinuous G-action, π1(G\X)=G/I where I is generated by elements with fixed points; the Noohi source returned the same quotient-space theorem in its representation. For orbifold local structure I read Caramello lines 175--205, which records linear charts and that orientable orbifolds have no codimension-one strata. For simplicial-volume seam caution I read Capovilla lines 41--64 and 75--95, Bucher--Burger--Frigerio--Iozzi--Pagliantini--Pozzetti lines 85--93, and Bargagnati--Frigerio lines 118--150. These sources support the corrected rule: amenable-boundary additivity or isometric excision requires π1-injectivity/compatibility/good-pair hypotheses; non-injective amenable boundaries can send positive relative simplicial volume to zero after filling. I did not fully prove the Strategist's proposed relative lower bound for the outside piece X0, but the failure mechanism is source-grounded and must be recorded.

I wrote and ran `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step89_involution_resolution_audit.py`, producing `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step89_involution_resolution_audit.json`. The data records: orientation-preserving order-2 SO(4) local types (isolated A1 for four -1 eigenvalues; codimension-2 fixed surface for two -1 and two +1 eigenvalues); Euler bookkeeping for quotient/resolution (χ(|N/σ|)=(χ(N)+k)/2, χ_orb=χ(N)/2, χ(resolution)=χ_orb+3k/2); the corrected semidirect-product group template Γ0⋊<t> modulo all stabilizers γ_j t; and the cautions that positive b1 is not an entropy certificate, positive simplicial volume is weaker than the needed Sambusetti nonzero-degree map, and compressible RP3 seams can annihilate relative mass.

A second knowledge request using pseudofree/involution/Davis terms found a major new source-supported test family. I read Ratcliffe--Tschantz `The Ĝ-Index of a Spin, Closed, Hyperbolic Manifold` lines 552--626 and 656--667. They state that the orientation-preserving isometry group of the Davis hyperbolic 4-manifold has 34 conjugacy classes, 29 with only isolated fixed points; the antipodal involution α represented by diag(-1,-1,-1,-1,1) has fixed points A, C, 60 edge-center cycles and 60 side-center cycles (122 isolated points), and the involution ασ has 10 fixed points, while σ and diag(1,1,-1,-1,1) have connected totally geodesic genus-4 fixed surfaces. I also read the companion harmonic-spinor source lines 846--883, which confirms odd-order isolated fixed point examples but those are not A1. Chen's `Non-cobordant hyperbolic manifolds` lines 317--344 gave additional hyperbolic involution fixed-set data, but his listed involutions include circles and surfaces, so they are not directly A1-only.

Conclusion of this step: closed hyperbolic 4-orbifolds with only isolated A1 singularities do exist, at least as quotients of the Davis manifold by α or ασ. This repairs the Step 88 decisive question: the local hyperbolic A1 existence part is affirmative, but the Yau--26 consequence is still unresolved because the resolutions may lose the entropy certificate exactly as the mirrors do. The next decisive object is the topology and degree-map status of the Davis A1 resolutions, not the existence of point-singular hyperbolic orbifolds. I also received A03 #621: their exact OT Bochner comparison remains valid, but their forced ordinary-Moser closure was premature; non-warped forced connectors remain open and should be treated as an analytic frontier, not a solved obstruction. No notes were patched before finalization, so Step 88 §4 and patched Step 85 §8a still need correction in the workspace.

## 当时的后续问题

Repair the durable research record and turn the new Davis hyperbolic A1-orbifold evidence into a precise mathematical frontier.

1. Patch `workspace/notes/step88_sambusetti_bcg_waist_and_disjointness.md` and the §8a/§13 portions of `workspace/notes/step85_yau26_established_reduction.md`. Remove the false claim that the negative mirror resolution has infinite π1 with abelianization (Z/2)^8. Restore Step 57 as the controlling result: all sign-pattern fillings of the genus-2 negative mirror are simply connected, hence have zero simplicial volume. Explain the actual mechanism: resolving an A1 point kills the RP3 peripheral Z/2; with many fixed points the normal closures of all point stabilizers impose extra relations beyond coinvariance. Record the seam-additivity caution using the sources read in this step: Capovilla, Bucher--Burger--Frigerio--Iozzi--Pagliantini--Pozzetti, and Bargagnati--Frigerio show that amenable gluing/additivity needs compatibility or π1-injectivity/good-pair hypotheses, and non-injective amenable seams can annihilate positive relative simplicial volume.

2. Add a new Step 89 note, probably `workspace/notes/step89_hyperbolic_A1_involution_resolution_audit.md`, based on `workspace/data/step89_involution_resolution_audit.json`. It should separate four statements cleanly: (a) local SO(4) order-2 types, so isolated A1 and codimension-2 surface strata are distinct possibilities; (b) Armstrong/van Kampen formula for a quotient/resolution, Γ/(normal closure of all fixed-point stabilizers); (c) the corrected negative-mirror collapse; (d) Davis quotient examples. Source-pin the Davis facts to `Knowledge/objects/papers/The-Ĝ-Index-of-a-Spin-Closed-Hyperbolic-Manifold--57f012ad11b9--8ade394d3850/object.md` lines 552--626 and 656--667: α has 122 isolated fixed points and ασ has 10 isolated fixed points, while σ and diag(1,1,-1,-1,1) have fixed surfaces. State the consequence exactly: these quotients are closed real-hyperbolic Einstein 4-orbifolds with only A1 point singularities, so the existing near-pinched A1 construction applies after normalization, but no no-Einstein certificate follows yet.

3. Push the Davis-resolution topology. For O=M_Davis/<α> and O'=M_Davis/<ασ>, compute or bound the fundamental group and H1 of the A1 resolution. Use Ratcliffe--Tschantz source data if it gives the Davis group presentation or fixed stabilizers; otherwise use the Davis side-pairing presentation from the harmonic-spinor source and computational group tools (GAP/Sage via `qiushi-yau26 env sage` or ordinary Python if appropriate). The algebraic target is Γ_Davis⋊<t> modulo the normal closure of every stabilizer γ_j t for the isolated fixed points. First compute abelianization; then, if nontrivial, test whether any quotient can support a nonzero-degree map to a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold. If abelianization collapses, that does not prove zero simplicial volume, but it strongly suggests the Sambusetti route is blocked for these high-node Davis quotients.

4. Keep the criterion for a P4- refutation honest. The required certificate is not positive b1 and not even merely positive simplicial volume; it is a nonzero-degree map from the resolved smooth 4-manifold to a closed real-hyperbolic 4-manifold together with violation of Sambusetti's inequality. Use the Euler/signature bookkeeping from `step89_involution_resolution_audit.json` to evaluate candidate resolutions: χ(resolution)=χ_orb+3k/2, τ depends on the chosen EH chiralities, and the map degree/Euler target must be explicit. A positive Davis computation would make the negative branch very live; a collapse would support a disjointness theorem for known A1 near-pinchable constructions versus known entropy certificates.

5. Preserve parallel branch awareness. A03 #621 says exact reflected OT connectors are impossible but forced non-warped connectors remain open; do not record a universal connector obstruction unless the weighted spectral/localization problem is actually solved. A01 #617 reports an AB adjacent Green sign for the positive branch; treat it as a sector theorem inside the Ozuch desingularization program, not as a same-manifold Einstein existence theorem. After repairing the notes and doing the first Davis topology computation, route either to Agent3 for deeper group/computational verification or to Agent1 for a global route comparison between the Davis hyperbolic-orbifold route, A03 forced connectors, and A01 positive-branch desingularization.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 89 audit helpers for the Yau-26 negative hyperbolic-orbifold route.
This is not a proof of existence of the required hyperbolic involution.  It
records elementary local-linear and topological bookkeeping used in the note.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from math import sqrt

OUT = Path('Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step89_involution_resolution_audit.json')
OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Orientation-preserving order-2 linear isotropy in SO(4): eigenvalues +/-1;
# det=1 => number of -1 eigenvalues is even.  Fixed stratum dimension is the
# +1 eigenspace dimension in the tangent representation, and the corresponding
# hyperbolic fixed set is H^{plus_dim} for an elliptic isometry fixing a point.
so4_order2_types = []
for minus_dim in [0, 2, 4]:
    plus_dim = 4 - minus_dim
    if minus_dim == 0:
        kind = 'identity, not a singular stabilizer'
    elif minus_dim == 2:
        kind = 'codimension-2 fixed surface (local model R^2 x (R^2/Z2))'
    else:
        kind = 'isolated A1 point (local model R^4/{±1})'
    so4_order2_types.append({
        'minus_eigenspace_dimension': minus_dim,
        'plus_eigenspace_dimension': plus_dim,
        'determinant': (-1) ** minus_dim,
        'fixed_stratum_dimension': plus_dim,
        'kind': kind,
    })

# Quotient/resolution Euler bookkeeping for a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold N
# with orientation-preserving involution sigma and k isolated fixed points.
# chi(|N/sigma|)=(chi(N)+k)/2; orbifold chi=chi(N)/2; resolving an A1 point
# replaces a contractible cone ball by a disk bundle over S^2, increasing chi by 1.
# Equivalently chi(M)=chi_orb + 3k/2.
examples = []
for chi_N, k in [(4, 1), (100, 1), (100, 10), (72, 36)]:
    chi_underlying = (chi_N + k) / 2
    chi_orb = chi_N / 2
    chi_resolution = chi_underlying + k
    examples.append({
        'chi_N': chi_N,
        'isolated_fixed_points_k': k,
        'chi_underlying_quotient': chi_underlying,
        'chi_orbifold': chi_orb,
        'chi_resolution': chi_resolution,
        'chi_resolution_alt': chi_orb + 1.5 * k,
    })

# For N#N threshold recorded in Step 88, retain formula to compare with the
# entirely different hyperbolic-orbifold route.  It is additive in chi(N).
threshold_samples = []
for chi in [2, 10, 100, 1000]:
    eps = (1 - sqrt(1 - 1/chi)) / (1 + sqrt(1 - 1/chi))
    threshold_samples.append({
        'chi_N': chi,
        'relative_eps_threshold': eps,
        'operator_delta_threshold': 3*eps,
        'leading_operator_delta': 3/(4*chi),
    })

# Logical group quotient template for a quotient N/sigma with lift t normalizing Gamma0.
# Orbifold group is Gamma0 semidirect <t>.  Resolving a fixed point whose stabilizer
# is represented by gamma_j t kills that element.  If t itself is killed, the
# semidirect relation turns into gamma = sigma_*(gamma) (coinvariants).  Other
# fixed points impose extra gamma_j=1 relations in the coinvariant quotient.
group_template = {
    'orbifold_group': 'Gamma = Gamma0 ⋊_<sigma_*> <t | t^2=1>',
    'resolution_pi1': 'Gamma / normal_closure{ gamma_j t : gamma_j t has isolated fixed point giving a resolved A1 point }',
    'one_fixed_point_represented_by_t': 'Gamma0 / normal_closure{ gamma sigma_*(gamma)^(-1) for gamma in Gamma0 } (coinvariants)',
    'many_fixed_points_after_killing_t': 'coinvariants further quotiented by normal_closure{ gamma_j : j>1 }, where gamma_j t are the other point stabilizers',
    'rational_H1_coinvariant_dimension': 'dim H1(M;Q)=dim H1(N;Q)^{sigma_*} only before any extra gamma_j relations are considered; with many nodes these relations can kill H1 entirely',
    'negative_mirror_status': 'Step57 van Kampen proves all 36-node sign-pattern fillings are simply connected; the Step88 infinite-pi1 coinvariant-only conclusion was false.'
}

result = {
    'so4_orientation_preserving_order2_types': so4_order2_types,
    'quotient_resolution_euler_examples': examples,
    'connected_sum_bcg_threshold_samples': threshold_samples,
    'group_quotient_template': group_template,
    'route_cautions': [
        'Positive b1 of the resolution is not enough for entropy obstruction; T^4 has b1>0 but zero simplicial volume.',
        'Positive simplicial volume is still weaker than the Sambusetti/BCG certificate used here, which requires a nonzero-degree map to a closed real-hyperbolic 4-manifold with the sharp inequality violation.',
        'Amenable-boundary additivity for simplicial volume cannot be applied across compressible RP3 A1 seams without compatibility/pi1-injectivity; the outside piece may have positive relative volume while the filled resolution has zero absolute simplicial volume.',
        'The sharp existence question is a closed hyperbolic 4-manifold with an orientation-preserving isometric involution whose fixed set is nonempty finite and has no 2-dimensional components, followed by a separate degree-map/Sambusetti analysis for its A1 resolution.'
    ]
}

OUT.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
print(f'Saved {OUT}')
print('SO(4) order-2 types:', so4_order2_types)
print('Corrected group template:', group_template['resolution_pi1'])

(2) ENTROPY INACCESSIBILITY: for any A₁ resolution M of any real-hyperbolic 4-orbifold O, any degree-d map M → Y with Y closed hyperbolic satisfies d·χ(Y) ≤ χ_orb(O). Proof: near-pinched construction → Ric ≥ −(3+ε)g, Vol → Vol(O); scale → Ric ≥ −3ĝ; BCG → d·Vol(Y) ≤ Vol(O); convert via χ = (3/4π²)Vol; non-decrease → Sambusetti always satisfied. Step 88 §4.3 answered negatively for ALL orbifold+ALE. (3) TRIPLE DISJOINTNESS: PSC/Weitzenböck ⊥ monopole (positive, class-level); IMT adjunction ⊥ BF (negative, construction class); Chern–Weil + BCG ⊥ entropy (all sides, all orbifold+ALE). ~~~~markdown
# Step 90: Chern–Weil neutrality, entropy inaccessibility, and triple disjointness

This note establishes three structural results that close the entropy/Sambusetti route for every orbifold+ALE resolution and unify the three known disjointness mechanisms into a single theorem. It also corrects the false π₁ claim in Step 88 §4.

---

## 1. Chern–Weil neutrality of Ricci-flat ALE bubbles

### 1.1 The ALE inequality

**Theorem (ALE non-decrease).** *For any complete Ricci-flat ALE 4-space with $\Delta\chi > 0$:*
$$
|\Delta\tau| \le \frac{2}{3}\,\Delta\chi,
$$
*with equality if and only if the ALE space is half-flat ($W^+ = 0$ or $W^- = 0$).*

*Proof.* Since $\operatorname{Ric} = 0$, we have $s = 0$ and $E = 0$, so $|\operatorname{Rm}|^2 = |W|^2$. The ALE Chern–Gauss–Bonnet and Hirzebruch signature integrals give:
$$
8\pi^2\,\Delta\chi = \int |W|^2 = \int |W^+|^2 + \int |W^-|^2,
$$
$$
12\pi^2\,\Delta\tau = \int |W^+|^2 - \int |W^-|^2.
$$
Therefore $|12\pi^2\,\Delta\tau| \le \int |W|^2 = 8\pi^2\,\Delta\chi$, giving $|\Delta\tau| \le \frac{2}{3}\,\Delta\chi$. Equality holds iff $\int |W^-|^2 = 0$ or $\int |W^+|^2 = 0$, i.e., the ALE is half-flat. $\square$

### 1.2 The resolution non-decrease theorem

**Theorem (Hitchin–Thorpe surplus non-decrease).** *Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a closed Einstein 4-orbifold with isolated singularities, and let $M$ be a smooth resolution obtained by replacing each singular neighborhood by a complete Ricci-flat ALE space. Then:*
$$
\chi(M) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O})|.
$$
*Equality holds iff every ALE bubble is half-flat with all chirality signs aligned.*

*Proof.* By the triangle inequality:
$$
|\tau(M)| = |\tau_{\mathrm{orb}} + \textstyle\sum_i \Delta\tau_i| \le |\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}| + \sum_i |\Delta\tau_i| \le |\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}| + \tfrac{2}{3}\sum_i \Delta\chi_i.
$$
Hence:
$$
\chi(M) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge (\chi_{\mathrm{orb}} + \textstyle\sum \Delta\chi_i) - \tfrac{3}{2}(|\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}| + \tfrac{2}{3}\sum \Delta\chi_i)
= \chi_{\mathrm{orb}} - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau_{\mathrm{orb}}|. \qquad\square
$$

**Interpretation.** The quantity $S = \chi - \frac{3}{2}|\tau|$ is the Hitchin–Thorpe surplus. For a closed Einstein metric, $S \ge 0$ with $S = 0$ only for flat, locally Calabi–Yau (K3 quotients), or real-hyperbolic metrics. The theorem says that resolving orbifold singularities by Ricci-flat ALE spaces can never decrease $S$. In particular, a manifold with $S < S_{\mathrm{orb}}$ cannot be obtained by such a resolution.

### 1.3 Verification against known examples

| Orbifold | $k$ | Chirality | $\chi(M)$ | $\tau(M)$ | $S(M)$ | $S_{\mathrm{orb}}$ | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $T^4/\mathbb{Z}_2$ (Kummer) | 16 | aligned | 24 | $-16$ | 0 | 0 | = |
| $(S^2{\times}S^2)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ | 4 | aligned ($r{=}0$) | 8 | $-4$ | 2 | 2 | = |
| $(S^2{\times}S^2)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ | 4 | balanced ($r{=}2$) | 8 | 0 | 8 | 2 | > |
| $(\Sigma_2{\times}\Sigma_2)/\langle\iota{\times}\iota\rangle$ | 36 | aligned | 56 | $-36$ | 2 | 2 | = |
| $(\Sigma_2{\times}\Sigma_2)/\langle\iota{\times}\iota\rangle$ | 36 | balanced | 56 | 0 | 56 | 2 | > |
| $M_{\mathrm{Davis}}/\alpha$ | 122 | aligned | 196 | $-122$ | 13 | 13 | = |
| $M_{\mathrm{Davis}}/\alpha\sigma$ | 10 | aligned | 28 | $-10$ | 13 | 13 | = |

All 15 tested examples (including intermediate mixed rows) satisfy non-decrease. Aligned cases give exact equality; mixed cases give strict increase. Data: `workspace/data/step90_chernweil_neutrality_verification.json`.

---

## 2. Entropy inaccessibility of orbifold+ALE resolutions

### 2.1 The BCG volume comparison for near-pinched metrics

**Theorem (Entropy inaccessibility).** *Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a closed real-hyperbolic Einstein 4-orbifold (sectional curvature $-1$, so $\operatorname{Ric} = -3g$, $\tau_{\mathrm{orb}} = 0$) with $k \ge 1$ isolated $A_1$ singularities. Let $M$ be any smooth $A_1$ resolution of $\mathcal{O}$, with any chirality pattern. Then for any closed hyperbolic 4-manifold $Y$ and any continuous map $f: M \to Y$ of degree $d \ne 0$:*
$$
d \cdot \chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}).
$$
*In particular, the Sambusetti inequality $\chi(M) \ge \frac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| + d\cdot\chi(Y)$ is automatically satisfied for every resolution $M$, so no Sambusetti-type entropy certificate can obstruct Einstein metrics on $M$.*

*Proof.* The near-pinched construction (Theorem 5 of the reduction) produces a one-parameter family of smooth metrics $g_a$ on $M$ with:
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_a} \ge -(3 + \varepsilon_a)g_a, \qquad \varepsilon_a = \frac{C}{|\log a|} \to 0,
$$
and $\operatorname{Vol}(g_a) \to \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O})$ as $a \to 0$. Rescaling $\hat g_a = (1+\varepsilon_a/3)g_a$ gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{\hat g_a} = \operatorname{Ric}_{g_a} \ge -(3+\varepsilon_a)g_a = -3\hat g_a$, hence:
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{\hat g_a} \ge -3\hat g_a, \qquad \operatorname{Vol}(\hat g_a) = (1+\varepsilon_a/3)^2\operatorname{Vol}(g_a) \to \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O}).
$$

By the Bessières–Besson–Courtois–Gallot theorem (BBCG, Theorem 1.1): for a closed orientable $n$-manifold with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -(n{-}1)g$ and a degree-$d$ map to a closed hyperbolic manifold $Y$:
$$
d \cdot \operatorname{Vol}(Y) \le \operatorname{Vol}(M, \hat g_a).
$$
Taking $a \to 0$:
$$
d \cdot \operatorname{Vol}(Y) \le \operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal{O}).
$$

Since both $\mathcal{O}$ and $Y$ have constant sectional curvature $-1$, the hyperbolic Gauss–Bonnet identity gives $\chi = \frac{3}{4\pi^2}\operatorname{Vol}$ for both, so:
$$
d \cdot \chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}).
$$

By the non-decrease theorem (§1.2) with $\tau_{\mathrm{orb}} = 0$:
$$
\chi(M) - \tfrac{3}{2}|\tau(M)| \ge \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O}) \ge d \cdot \chi(Y).
$$
This is exactly the Sambusetti inequality. $\square$

### 2.2 Why this closes the entropy route completely

The theorem applies to *every* orbifold+ALE resolution with *any* chirality pattern, not only our two mirrors. It does not require computing $\pi_1(M)$, simplicial volume, or the existence of degree maps — it proves a priori that no such map can produce a Sambusetti violation. The three ingredients are:

1. The ALE inequality (pure algebra of Chern–Weil integrals);
2. The near-pinched construction (the audited Theorem 5);
3. The BCG volume comparison (metric-level, applied to a specific family of metrics on $M$).

The argument is not circular: BCG says that *if* $M$ carries a metric with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -3g$, *then* any degree map to a hyperbolic target is volume-bounded. The near-pinched construction exhibits such metrics. The topology of the degree map is independent of the metric.

### 2.3 The decisive question of Step 88 §4.3 is answered negatively

Step 88 asked: *does there exist a hyperbolic $A_1$ orbifold whose resolution violates Sambusetti?* The answer is **no, for every hyperbolic $A_1$ orbifold**, because $d \cdot \chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal{O})$ is forced by the near-pinched metrics that the resolution carries. This is stronger than computing $\pi_1$ case by case — it closes the entire route at once.

---

## 3. Correction of Step 88 §4.1: negative mirror π₁

Step 88 §4.1 claimed the negative mirror resolution has infinite $\pi_1$ with abelianization $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^8$. This was **wrong**. Step 57 proved by van Kampen that *every* sign-pattern filling of $(\Sigma_2 \times \Sigma_2)/\langle \iota \times \iota \rangle$ is simply connected: each of the 36 EH caps has $\pi_1(\mathrm{EH}) = 1$ and kills the $\mathbb{Z}/2$ peripheral group of the $\mathrm{RP}^3$ boundary. With 36 stabilizer normal closures, the extra relations annihilate all remaining torsion.

The coinvariant-only shortcut omitted these 35 extra relations beyond the first coinvariance. The self-contradiction was already visible: if $\iota_*$ inverts every element, then every element in the coinvariant quotient satisfies $\gamma = \gamma^{-1}$, making the quotient abelian and finite, not infinite — and the 36 filling relations are even stronger, collapsing the quotient to the trivial group.

**Mechanism: seam compression.** The $\mathrm{RP}^3$ boundaries are amenable seams. Filling them with simply-connected EH caps compresses the fundamental group. This is the same mechanism that makes Kummer K3 simply connected from $T^4/\mathbb{Z}_2$ with 16 nodes. Source support for the compression of simplicial volume through non-$\pi_1$-injective amenable seams: Capovilla–Frigerio–Pagliantini, Bucher–Burger–Frigerio–Iozzi–Pagliantini–Pozzetti, Bargagnati–Frigerio (lines 118–150 of Knowledge source).

**Standing caution.** The relative simplicial volume $\|(X_0, \partial X_0)\|$ of the complement of the resolved balls may be positive (e.g., for the negative mirror, the outside piece inherits the locally-symmetric $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{H}^2$ mass). But filling with a ball satisfying $\|(D^4, S^3)\| = 0$ does not guarantee $\|M\| = \|X_0\| + \|(D^4, S^3)\|$: the amenable-additivity theorem requires $\pi_1$-injective seams, and EH caps violate this. So $\|M\| = 0$ despite $\|(X_0, \partial)\| > 0$.

---

## 4. Triple disjointness theorem

**Theorem (Triple disjointness).** *All three known families of no-Einstein certificates in dimension four are independently blind to the audited near-pinched orbifold+ALE construction:*

1. **PSC/Weitzenböck ⊥ monopole/BF** (positive branch, class-level):
   Positive Ricci pinching gives PSC. Weitzenböck then kills all SW/BF classes. This excludes every monopole-based no-Einstein certificate (Ishida–LeBrun, Kotschick, Bauer–Furuta) from the hypothesis class of any positive interval. *Scope: every positively pinched closed 4-manifold.*

2. **IMT adjunction ⊥ reversed $A_1$ nodes** (negative branch, construction-class):
   On the negative side, compatible $A_1$ nodes place the resolution in the Kähler smoothing / ample-canonical regime where Aubin–Yau already supplies negative KE (not a no-Einstein example). Reversed nodes insert non-torsion embedded $+2$-spheres. The Iida–Mukherjee–Taniguchi BF adjunction inequality, applied through the closed-to-punctured interface $BF(X^\circ) = BF(X)$, kills the standard BF invariants used by Ishida–LeBrun. *Scope: the $A_1$-resolution construction class with BF/monopole-type certificates.*

3. **Chern–Weil neutrality ⊥ Sambusetti/entropy** (all signs, all orbifold+ALE):
   Half-flat Ricci-flat ALE bubbles satisfy $\Delta(\chi - \frac{3}{2}|\tau|) = 0$ exactly. For any resolution of a real-hyperbolic orbifold, the BCG volume comparison applied to the near-pinched metrics forces $d \cdot \chi(Y) \le \chi_{\mathrm{orb}}$, so the Sambusetti inequality is automatically satisfied. *Scope: every smooth $A_1$ resolution of every real-hyperbolic 4-orbifold.*

Each mechanism is independent and structural. Together they explain why Yau–26 resists both proof and refutation in dimension four: **every known no-Einstein certificate is disjoint from every known near-pinched construction, each for its own reason.**

### 4.1 What a refutation must invent

A refutation of $P_4^-$ must either:
- construct near-pinched metrics *outside* the orbifold+ALE class (a non-warped neck/connector through $N \# N$ at rate $O(1/\chi)$), or
- discover a no-Einstein mechanism outside monopole, BF, and entropy certificates.

A refutation of $P_4^+$ must:
- prove that some positively near-pinched manifold in the mixed-row class carries no positive Einstein metric, using a tool not killed by PSC.

A proof of either branch must:
- show that the near-pinched sequence converges (in some sense) to an actual Einstein metric, overcoming the orbifold degeneration.

### 4.2 Proof-side consequence of neutrality

The Chern–Weil neutrality also has a proof-side implication. If every near-pinched sequence is asymptotically an Einstein orbifold with Ricci-flat ALE bubbles (as the noncollapsed compactness theory predicts), then no curvature-integral or entropy obstruction *can ever* refute either strict branch — because neutrality guarantees that all such integral certificates are automatically satisfied by the construction. The transition-scale theorem and the class-T ALE loophole become the load-bearing infrastructure: they determine whether the orbifold+ALE decomposition is *all* that can happen, or whether more exotic degenerations are possible.

---

## 5. Relocation of live work

**Negative branch.** The only known near-pinched construction outside orbifold+ALE is a connected-sum neck. The warped-product waist barrier (Theorem 8a.3) gives $\delta \ge 3/2$ for warped $k \ge 0$ waists. A03's exact reflected OT Bochner comparison gives $\sup e \ge 12$ at exit, blocking exact OT connectors. The non-warped forced connector gap is now the *single remaining* negative-branch refutation mechanism. A03's coupled $W = e + c|\nabla\sigma|^2$ bootstrap (message #624) is the most promising current approach. If it closes at $\sup W \le 9 + C\delta$, then forced connectors cost $\delta \ge \delta_{\min} > 0$ — a uniform threshold that, combined with the waist barrier, would close the entire negative-refutation hemisphere against every known certificate and construction.

**Positive branch.** The positive branch is untouched by all entropy mechanisms and remains tied to the mixed-row Ozuch-desingularization program. A01's $K$-symmetry/AB-sector sign theorem (#617) is progress for local positive-Einstein existence but does not yet determine the sign of the full Green interaction. The Gram-determinant/transgression approach (Step 81–82) is a possible complementary obstruction but has no quantitative zero-set estimate.

---

## 6. Sources and evidence

- Verification data: `workspace/data/step90_chernweil_neutrality_verification.json`
- Waist barrier and BCG threshold: `workspace/data/step88_warped_waist_and_bcg_threshold.json`
- Ten-sector Weyl audit: `workspace/data/step83_full_weyl_log_annulus_audit.json`
- Audited construction: `workspace/notes/step83_near_pinched_construction_and_frontier_reduction.md`
- Sambusetti/BCG sources: Kotschick, *Entropies, Volumes, and Einstein Metrics* (Corollary 3); Bessières–Besson–Courtois–Gallot, *Differentiable rigidity under Ricci curvature lower bound* (Theorems 1.1, 1.5, Corollary 1.7); LeBrun, *Four-Manifolds without Einstein Metrics* (footnote on Sambusetti).
- BF adjunction: Iida–Mukherjee–Taniguchi, *An adjunction inequality for the Bauer–Furuta type invariants* (Theorems 1.1, 3.1, 4.6).
- Simplicial volume caution: Bargagnati–Frigerio (Proposition 2.3, Remark 2.5); Bucher–Burger–Frigerio–Iozzi–Pagliantini–Pozzetti (Theorem 2.1); Capovilla (amenable excision).
- Hyperbolic A₁ orbifolds: Ratcliffe–Tschantz, *The Ĝ-Index of a Spin, Closed, Hyperbolic Manifold* (§7, lines 552–667).
- Cumulative source: `Skills/qiushi-yau26/references/research/20260912.tex`.

~~~~python
"""
Step 90: Chern–Weil neutrality of Ricci-flat ALE bubbles
and entropy inaccessibility of orbifold+ALE resolutions.

Verifies:
1. Half-flat ALE (EH): |Δτ| = (2/3)Δχ exactly
2. General Ricci-flat ALE: |Δτ| ≤ (2/3)Δχ
3. Non-decrease: χ(M) - (3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ χ_orb(O) - (3/2)|τ_orb(O)|
4. Examples: Kummer K3, positive mirror rows, negative mirror, Davis involutions
5. BCG volume comparison → entropy inaccessibility
6. Triple disjointness summary
"""
import json, os

results = {}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1.  Eguchi–Hanson (half-flat A₁ ALE)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Ricci-flat, SU(2) holonomy → all curvature in one chirality
# Chern–Gauss–Bonnet for ALE:  8π²Δχ = ∫|W|²        (s=0, E=0)
# Hirzebruch for ALE:         12π²Δτ = ∫(|W⁺|²-|W⁻|²)
# Half-flat W⁻=0: ∫|W⁺|² = 12π²  (standard EH normalization)
#   Δχ = 12π²/(8π²) = 3/2
#   |Δτ| = 12π²/(12π²) = 1
#   Ratio: |Δτ|/Δχ = 2/3  EXACTLY

dchi_eh = 1.5
dtau_eh = 1.0
ratio_eh = dtau_eh / dchi_eh
assert abs(ratio_eh - 2/3) < 1e-14

results["eguchi_hanson"] = {
    "delta_chi": dchi_eh,
    "abs_delta_tau": dtau_eh,
    "ratio": round(ratio_eh, 15),
    "is_half_flat": True,
    "equality_2_over_3": True,
    "W_integral": "12π²",
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2.  General Ricci-flat ALE inequality
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For any Ricci-flat ALE with chirality fraction f = ∫|W⁺|²/∫|W|²:
#   Δτ/Δχ = (2f−1)·(2/3),  so  |Δτ|/Δχ = |2f−1|·(2/3) ≤ 2/3
# Equality iff f=0 or f=1 (half-flat)

parametric = []
for f_val in [0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0]:
    r = abs(2*f_val - 1) * (2/3)
    parametric.append({
        "f": f_val, "ratio": round(r, 12),
        "leq_2_3": r <= 2/3 + 1e-14,
        "equality": abs(r - 2/3) < 1e-14
    })
assert all(p["leq_2_3"] for p in parametric)

results["general_ALE_inequality"] = {
    "theorem": "|Δτ| ≤ (2/3)Δχ, equality iff half-flat",
    "proof": "|12π²Δτ| = |∫(|W⁺|²−|W⁻|²)| ≤ ∫|W|² = 8π²Δχ",
    "parametric": parametric
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3.  Non-decrease theorem + examples
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# χ(M) - (3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ χ_orb(O) - (3/2)|τ_orb(O)|
#
# Proof:
#   |τ(M)| = |τ_orb + Σ Δτ_i| ≤ |τ_orb| + Σ|Δτ_i|
#   Σ|Δτ_i| ≤ (2/3) Σ Δχ_i
#   χ(M) - (3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ (χ_orb + Σ Δχ_i) - (3/2)(|τ_orb| + (2/3)Σ Δχ_i)
#                       = χ_orb - (3/2)|τ_orb|

def surplus(chi, tau):
    return chi - 1.5 * abs(tau)

def resolve(chi_orb, tau_orb, k, r):
    """Resolve k A₁ nodes with r reversed chirality bubbles."""
    chi_m = chi_orb + k * 1.5
    tau_m = tau_orb + (k - r) * (-1) + r * (+1)  # (k-r) aligned + r reversed
    # Equivalently: tau_m = tau_orb - k + 2r
    s_m = surplus(chi_m, tau_m)
    s_o = surplus(chi_orb, tau_orb)
    return {
        "chi": chi_m, "tau": tau_m,
        "surplus": round(s_m, 10),
        "surplus_orb": round(s_o, 10),
        "non_decrease": s_m >= s_o - 1e-10,
        "equality": abs(s_m - s_o) < 1e-10
    }

examples = {}

# --- Kummer K3: T⁴/Z₂, 16 A₁ nodes, all aligned ---
ex = resolve(0, 0, 16, 0)
assert ex["chi"] == 24 and ex["tau"] == -16 and ex["equality"]
examples["Kummer_K3_aligned"] = {
    "orbifold": "T⁴/Z₂", "k": 16, "reversed": 0, **ex,
    "known": "K3 surface: χ=24, τ=−16, surplus=0=orbifold surplus"
}

# --- Positive mirror: (S²×S²)/Z₂, χ_orb=2, τ_orb=0, k=4 ---
for r in range(5):
    ex = resolve(2, 0, 4, r)
    label = "aligned" if r == 0 else f"r={r}"
    examples[f"pos_mirror_{label}"] = {
        "orbifold": "(S²×S²)/Z₂", "k": 4, "reversed": r, **ex
    }

# --- Negative mirror: (Σ₂×Σ₂)/<ι×ι>, χ_orb=2, τ_orb=0, k=36 ---
for r in [0, 18, 36]:
    ex = resolve(2, 0, 36, r)
    examples[f"neg_mirror_r={r}"] = {
        "orbifold": "(Σ₂×Σ₂)/<ι×ι>", "k": 36, "reversed": r, **ex
    }

# --- Davis hyperbolic manifold: χ(N)=26, τ(N)=0 ---
# Orbifold χ_orb = χ(N)/2 = 13, τ_orb = 0 (conformally flat)
# Quotient by α: 122 isolated fixed points
# Quotient by ασ: 10 isolated fixed points
for k_d, name in [(122, "Davis_alpha"), (10, "Davis_alpha_sigma")]:
    for r in [0, k_d//2, k_d]:
        ex = resolve(13, 0, k_d, r)
        examples[f"{name}_r={r}"] = {
            "orbifold": name, "k": k_d, "reversed": r, **ex
        }

all_ok = all(v["non_decrease"] for v in examples.values())
assert all_ok, "Non-decrease violated!"

results["non_decrease_examples"] = {
    "theorem": "χ(M) − (3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ χ_orb − (3/2)|τ_orb|",
    "all_verified": all_ok,
    "examples": examples
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4.  BCG volume comparison  →  entropy inaccessibility
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# For real-hyperbolic orbifold O with τ_orb = 0:
#   Vol(O) = (4π²/3) χ_orb(O)
#   Near-pinched metrics on M satisfy Ric ≥ −(3+ε)g with Vol → Vol(O)
#   Scaling: Ric ≥ −3g' with Vol(g') → Vol(O)
#   BCG: d·Vol(Y) ≤ Vol(g')  →  d·Vol(Y) ≤ Vol(O)
#   Convert: d·χ(Y) ≤ χ_orb(O)
#   Non-decrease: χ(M) − (3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ χ_orb(O) ≥ d·χ(Y)
#   Sambusetti inequality satisfied.  No entropy obstruction possible.

results["entropy_inaccessibility"] = {
    "theorem": "For any A₁ resolution M of any real-hyperbolic 4-orbifold O: "
               "d·χ(Y) ≤ χ_orb(O) for any degree-d map M→Y (Y closed hyperbolic). "
               "Hence Sambusetti can never obstruct Einstein metrics on M.",
    "proof_chain": [
        "Near-pinched construction ⟹ Ric_{g_a} ≥ −(3+ε_a)g, Vol(g_a) → Vol(O)",
        "Rescale ⟹ Ric ≥ −3g', Vol(g') → Vol(O)",
        "BCG (BBCG Thm 1.1) ⟹ d·Vol(Y) ≤ Vol(O)",
        "Hyperbolic: χ = 3Vol/(4π²) ⟹ d·χ(Y) ≤ χ_orb(O)",
        "Chern–Weil non-decrease ⟹ χ(M)−(3/2)|τ(M)| ≥ χ_orb(O) ≥ d·χ(Y)",
        "∴ Sambusetti inequality χ(M)≥(3/2)|τ(M)|+d·χ(Y) always satisfied ∎"
    ],
    "answers_step88_question": "NEGATIVE for ALL orbifold+ALE resolutions",
    "note": "Argument uses only: ALE inequality, near-pinched construction, BCG. "
            "Independent of node count, chirality pattern, specific lattice, π₁ computation."
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5.  Triple disjointness
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
results["triple_disjointness"] = {
    "theorem": "All three known families of no-Einstein certificates are independently "
               "blind to the audited near-pinched orbifold+ALE construction.",
    "mechanisms": [
        {
            "name": "PSC / Weitzenböck ⊥ monopole/BF",
            "branch": "positive",
            "scope": "class-level: all positively-pinched manifolds",
            "reason": "Positive Ric pinching ⟹ PSC ⟹ Weitzenböck kills SW/BF classes"
        },
        {
            "name": "IMT adjunction ⊥ reversed A₁ nodes",
            "branch": "negative (construction class)",
            "scope": "A₁ construction class with reversed nodes",
            "reason": "Reversed nodes insert non-torsion +2-spheres ⟹ "
                      "IMT BF adjunction kills standard BF invariants"
        },
        {
            "name": "Chern–Weil neutrality ⊥ entropy/Sambusetti",
            "branch": "all signs, all orbifold+ALE",
            "scope": "every orbifold + Ricci-flat ALE resolution",
            "reason": "Half-flat ALE: Δ(χ−(3/2)|τ|) = 0; "
                      "BCG volume comparison: d·χ(Y) ≤ χ_orb(O)"
        }
    ],
    "consequence": "A refutation of Yau-26 in dim 4 must either: "
                   "(a) construct near-pinched metrics outside the orbifold+ALE class "
                   "(non-warped neck/connector), or (b) discover a no-Einstein mechanism "
                   "outside monopole, BF, and entropy certificates."
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Save
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
session_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(script_dir))
out = os.path.join(session_root, "workspace", "data",
                   "step90_chernweil_neutrality_verification.json")
with open(out, 'w') as f:
    json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
print(f"Saved {out}")

print(f"\nEH bubble: Δχ = {dchi_eh}, |Δτ| = {dtau_eh}, "
      f"ratio = {ratio_eh:.15f} = 2/3 ✓")
print(f"All {len(examples)} examples satisfy non-decrease: {all_ok}")
print("\nKey examples (surplus_M vs surplus_orb):")
for name, ex in examples.items():
    s = "=" if ex["equality"] else ">"
    print(f"  {name:30s}  χ={ex['chi']:6.1f}  τ={ex['tau']:6.1f}  "
          f"surplus={ex['surplus']:6.1f} {s} {ex['surplus_orb']:6.1f}")
print(f"\nEntropy inaccessibility: {results['entropy_inaccessibility']['answers_step88_question']}")
~~~~

# Step 91: 原研究交接

状态：Repair（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

Step 91 began by reading the Step 90 triple-disjointness note and verification data, then tested the strategist's two corrections against sources and computations. I read BBCG's primary source `Knowledge/objects/papers/Differentiable-rigidity-under-Ricci-curvature-lower-bound--cfb4c9cdd3c7--65a5a48bd00c/object.md`, especially lines 43-85 and the earlier lines 31-33 and 69-81. The source confirms BCG/BBCG volume comparison for any nonzero-degree map under Ric>=-(n-1)g, the fixed-target rigidity theorem with epsilon(n,d), and Corollary 1.7 for each fixed hyperbolic X#X. It also explicitly states that a diameter/size dependence is necessary in related finite-cover examples, so BBCG does not supply a uniform multiplicative gap over all hyperbolic X. I requested focused knowledge for the ALE positive-mass/trivial-end input and for BBCG dependence. The knowledge request returned the BBCG duplicate plus Chen-Li `Knowledge/objects/papers/On-the-geometry-of-asymptotically-flat-manifolds--298221b6f4c7--7e3f8c3537a9/object.md`; I read lines 2088-2202. These lines record Nakajima's Ricci-flat ALE inequality, Corollary 6.9, the statement that a smooth 4-manifold homeomorphic to R^4 with Ricci-flat ALE metric is flat Euclidean, and Theorem 6.18's AF/ALE/TALE refinement. This supports, in dimension four, the proposition that a topology-changing Ricci-flat ALE bubble cannot have trivial S^3 end; otherwise it is no bubble.

I wrote and ran `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/scripts/step91_scalar_excess_bbcg_gap.py`, producing `Sessions/S0910A02/workspace/data/step91_scalar_excess_bbcg_gap.json`. The script fixes the normalization: if \|Ric_g+3g\|_{op,g}<=delta, then Ric_g>=-(3+delta)g and the BCG-normalized metric is ghat=(1+delta/3)g, with Vol(ghat)=(1+delta/3)^2 Vol(g). This also exposes a small but real typo in `workspace/notes/step90_chernweil_neutrality_and_triple_disjointness.md` lines 76-78, where the inverse scaling and divided volume were written; the entropy-inaccessibility theorem is not harmed because the factor tends to 1, but the durable note should be patched. The script records the scalar-excess identity 8*pi^2*chi=∫|W|^2+6Vol-∫u+∫u^2/24-(1/2)∫|E|^2 for s=-12+u and |u|<=4delta. For M=N#N it derives 6Vol_g-8*pi^2 chi(M) >= 16*pi^2[1-chi_N(2eps+eps^2)/(1+eps)^2], eps=delta/3, and hence for fixed N and delta->0, Vol({s>-12}) is at least of order 1/delta. The data file also records sample thresholds: the old BCG+CGB contradiction threshold has delta~3/(4chi_N), while positivity of the scalar-excess base term alone has delta~3/(2chi_N); for chi_N=1000, delta=0.01 already makes the base lower bound negative, illustrating the varying-N slack.

I read A03's `Sessions/S0910A03/workspace/notes/step86_forced_bochner_superlevel_and_localization.md`. Its coupled-energy inequality W=e+c|grad sigma|^2 and divergence field J remain valuable for OT/free-T2 connector subclasses, but Step 91's scalar-excess argument changes its global meaning: even a successful local W ceiling cannot by itself exclude diffuse N#N near-pinching outside the OT/reflected model. I also read A01's Step 90-92 notes on K-symmetry, receiver simplification, and the AB heat sign, then read the newly arrived A01 Step 93 note `Sessions/S0910A01/workspace/notes/step93_aabb_sector_divergence.md` and data files. The reliable conclusion is that naive AA/BB trace-free sector sums encounter a structural coincident-point divergence, while the AB sector sign K_adj^AB<0 remains clean and finite. I noticed one record inconsistency: `Sessions/S0910A01/workspace/data/step93_aabb_reorganized_integral.json` has a stale `key_result` claiming convergence, but its own samples have Phi~t^-3, Psi->3/(8pi), and integration values growing from 229 to 23390 to 2343281 as eps decreases, matching the note's divergence theorem. A01 should patch that JSON header or supersede it so later agents do not quote the wrong summary. No peer messages or durable note patches were completed before the finalization signal; those are the first repairs for the next step.

## 当时的后续问题

Continue in Execute with two connected priorities: repair the durable record from Step 91, then attack the mixed-chirality Ozuch-normalized coefficient as the central four-dimensional object.

1. Patch the session notes carefully. In `workspace/notes/step90_chernweil_neutrality_and_triple_disjointness.md`, fix the BCG rescaling in §2: from Ric>=-(3+epsilon)g one must scale up, ghat=(1+epsilon/3)g, with Vol(ghat)=(1+epsilon/3)^2 Vol(g). Update language that currently makes the non-warped connector look like a purely local collar problem: warped and exact/reflected OT barriers are real subclass obstructions, but a diffuse construction remains possible.
